the coupling effect in a two-phase interleaved DC–DC converter with coupled inductor in discontinuous-current mode can be described by the equivalent inductor method, and the circuit status is determined by the physical relationship between input–output voltage and coupling coefficient.

The coupling effects on a two-phase interleaved converter in DCM are analyzed and the operation statuses are figured out, and the DCM operation conditions are derived and used to classify the modes, and ten DCM operation models are analyzed and the key parameters are figured out.
the coupling effect on the circuit status is described and three major circuit statuses according to the input–output ratio and coupling coefficient are figured out.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the DCM operation of a two-phase interleaved converter with a coupled-inductor, which is rarely reported in the literature.
the operation modes of a two-phase interleaved dc–dc converter, which can be applied to the design and control of a two-phase converter with a coupled-inductor in DCM.
the DCM operation of the two-phase interleaved DC–DC converter, and the analysis is useful to the design and application.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the DCM operation mode of an interleaved boost dc converter is determined by the coupling coefficient and the input–output ratio.
a two-phase interleaved DC–DC converter with a coupled-inductor in DCM can be operated in 10 operation modes, and the coupling effects on the converter operation are analyzed and discussed in detail.
the coupling effects are significant in a two-phase interleaved dc–dc converter in DCM, especially for the forced-conduction of the diode or MOSFET.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the DCM operation of a two-phase interleaved converter with a coupled-inductor is not as simple as that of a converter with an uncoupled inductor, and the analysis in this paper can be a good reference for the design, analysis, and control of such a DCM operation.
a two-phase interleaved converter with a coupled-inductor can be operated in a DCM, and the coupling effects on the converter operation can be analyzed and understood.
the analysis of the two-phase interleaved converter with coupled inductor is more complex than that of the converter with uncoupled inductor in DMC, but the analysis method is simple and effective.
The main takeaway from our work is that
coupling effects should be considered when a converter with a coupled-inductor is analyzed in DCM.

the coupled inductors in DCM operation modes can be used to achieve the voltage conversion ratio of 1.5 or more with only one inductor, and the coupling coefficient can be designed to achieve the maximum voltage conversion ratio.
